title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
seo_title: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 1 Intermediate Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Forces are pushes or pulls; contact and non-contact forces; balanced forces do not change motion, while unbalanced forces change speed or direction; weight and mass; friction. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 1, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): contact and field forces, effects of forces, balanced and unbalanced forces, weight and mass and friction. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons (N) with a spring balance. Contact forces act when objects touch (friction, tension, applied force). Field forces act at a distance (gravity, magnetic and electrostatic forces).

Weight is the force of gravity on a mass: W = mg, with g = 9,8 N·kg⁻¹ on Earth. Balanced forces cancel out, so the motion does not change; unbalanced forces make an object speed up, slow down or change direction.

Example

Is magnetism a contact force or a field force?

Magnets act without touching.

Answer: a field force

Example

What is the weight of a 10 kg bag on Earth?

W = mg

Answer: 98 N

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mass (kg) and weight (N).
  • Thinking a moving object needs a force to keep moving.
  • Thinking gravity only acts on falling objects.

items.q: Is this a contact force or a non-contact force: water pushing up on a floating boat?
c: a non-contact force (it acts at a distance)
items.e: Most forces need things to touch. Magnetism and gravity act at a distance.

items.q: What is the weight of a 10 kg object on the Moon, where g = 1.6 N/kg?

items.q: In which of these is friction useful?
c: a cyclist having to pedal harder on a rough road
carpet wearing thin where people walk
a match being struck to light it
the soles of shoes wearing out
items.e: Friction helps us grip, stop and write.

items.q: Which of these increases friction?
c: using ball bearings in a bicycle wheel
putting chalk on a gymnast's hands
putting wheels on a heavy suitcase
items.e: Rough or grippy surfaces increase friction.

items.q: In which of these is friction useful?
c: the moving parts of a machine getting hot
carpet wearing thin where people walk
the soles of shoes gripping the floor when we walk
a door hinge squeaking and being hard to open
items.e: Friction helps us grip, stop and write.

items.q: Which of these reduces friction?
c: putting wheels on a heavy suitcase
items.e: Lubricants, smooth surfaces, wheels and ball bearings reduce friction.

items.q: In which of these is friction a problem?
c: car tyres becoming smooth over time
our hands gripping a badminton racket
the soles of shoes gripping the floor when we walk
items.e: Friction wears surfaces away, produces heat and wastes energy.
